segments.text: Sunrise, near the top of Everest. A man sits in the snow. No hat. No gloves. He was declared dead last night.
Dead men don't sit up. No chance. Let's go look.
{2006|Two thousand six}. Lincoln Hall, an Australian climber, reaches the summit. On the way down, altitude sickness drops him.
His Sherpas fight for hours to save him. At dusk they are ordered down. His family is told he is dead.
He spends the night alone. No oxygen. No sleeping bag.
At dawn, four climbers find him. He says: I imagine you are surprised to see me here.
They give up their summit to stay with him. Sherpas climb up and bring him down.
He lost his fingertips and a toe. He called his book Dead Lucky.
Declared dead. Found making conversation. I was wrong. Case closed.
